scope.candidate_status: Diagnostic candidates only; neither implementation is adopted. No repository runtime edits were made.
scope.accuracy: No HPO, final-bank reuse, physical-system scoring or accuracy/generalization result. All workloads use a fresh synthetic development signal and previously fixed recipe.
scope.statistical_unit: Initial attribution: one fresh process/case, five repetitions after one warmup. Candidate diagnostics: two fresh processes each; ABBA pairs within a process are repeated observations, not independent hosts. Ranges are observed extrema, not confidence intervals.
scope.performance: Plain public timing is separate from cProfile/Torch profiler instrumentation. No cross-hardware, automatic-storage/default, compile or memory claim.
scope.reproduction: Exact scripts, source manifest, fixed seeds/recipe, actual native receipts and expected input/weight/output hashes are included. Checkpoints/full arrays are intentionally omitted. Regeneration can differ across library/hardware environments; hashes describe the captured experiment.
scope.encoding: Repeated identical native and import-origin receipts are stored once by SHA256; case/process records reference them. Hash uses json.dumps(value,sort_keys=True) UTF8. Raw timing samples and mode fingerprints remain inline.

protocol.scope: Fresh synthetic development signals, fixed known recipe; no search, tuning, scoring or final-bank access. Construction/eigen scaling is outside operation timings. Profile samples are separate and not latency evidence.

execution_boundaries.public_fit: rd.Model(graph=fixed_saved_graph,washout=case washout).fit(observations), including internal staged deepcopy, learned preprocessing, algebraic fit and commit. Outer construction/clone, eigen scaling, artifact I/O, policy checks and hashes outside clocks.
execution_boundaries.public_forecast: Original-unit history+forecast; compile=False, no hooks. Full complete prediction shape and finite checks; stored final state and fitted tensors fingerprinted.
execution_boundaries.readout: Explicit RidgeReadoutLayer(solver=cholesky,bias=False), alpha5.820835246142014e-11, matches actual equal-time budget adapter. AutoReadout/SVD are not this workload.
execution_boundaries.common_recurrence: Same projected streams and stored operator, complete sequence collection. Torch tanh+lerp is unchanged; NumPy/SciPy equations may round differently. No readout/input-projection cost inside this diagnostic.
execution_boundaries.csr_candidate: Only _recurrent replaced. Lazy SciPy CSR conversion/cache creation from actual Torch CSR components charged on first call per cell inside fit and forecast; numpy()/from_numpy() bridge charged every update.
execution_boundaries.b4_candidate: Only dense recurrent multiplication replaced with four per-row addmv operations and stack; activation/leak/readout/scaling/wrapper unchanged.

"""Fixed-input micro attribution only, not whole-workflow speed evidence."""
import hashlib,json,os,platform,statistics,sys,time
from pathlib import Path
BASE=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
import _threads as threads
threads.bootstrap_cli()
with threads.single_thread_policy() as policy:
 import numpy as np
 import scipy,scipy.sparse
 import torch
 with torch.no_grad():
  checkpoint=torch.load(BASE/'weights-1000.pt',weights_only=True)
  key=next(k for k,v in checkpoint.items() if isinstance(v,torch.Tensor) and tuple(v.shape)==(1000,1000))
  W=checkpoint[key];WT=W.t();csr=W.to_sparse_csr();npW=W.numpy();npCSR=scipy.sparse.csr_matrix(npW)
  rng=np.random.default_rng(90423)
  output={'schema':'cpu-fixed-primitive-attribution-v1','pid':os.getpid(),'native_policy':policy,'probe_sha256':hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'weight_key':key,'weight_values_sha256':hashlib.sha256(npW.tobytes()).hexdigest(),'scope':'Fixed input/kernel dispatch diagnostic.250calls/sample,7rotating-order rounds afterwarmup; no model/horizon/forecast improvement claim. All results materialized before hash/maxabs outside clocks.','rows':[]}
  for batch in (1,4):
   st=torch.tensor(rng.standard_normal((batch,1000)),dtype=torch.float64);p=torch.tensor(rng.standard_normal((batch,1000)),dtype=torch.float64)
   ns=st.numpy();npP=p.numpy();dest=torch.empty_like(p)
   variants={
    'torch_addmm':lambda:torch.addmm(p,st,WT),
    'torch_mm_plus':lambda:p+torch.mm(st,WT),
    'torch_transposed_mm_plus':lambda:p+torch.mm(W,st.t()).t(),
    'torch_rows_addmv_stack':lambda:torch.stack([torch.addmv(p[b],W,st[b]) for b in range(batch)]),
    'torch_csr_mm_plus':lambda:p+torch.sparse.mm(csr,st.t()).t(),
    'numpy_dense_plus':lambda:npP+ns@npW.T,
    'numpy_transposed_plus':lambda:npP+(npW@ns.T).T,
    'scipy_csr_plus':lambda:npP+(npCSR@ns.T).T,
    'torch_tanh':lambda:torch.tanh(p),
    'torch_tanh_out':lambda:torch.tanh(p,out=dest),
    'torch_clone_tanh_inplace':lambda:p.clone().tanh_(),
    'numpy_tanh':lambda:np.tanh(npP),
    'torch_lerp':lambda:torch.lerp(st,p,.38042233452564966),
    'numpy_leak':lambda:ns+.38042233452564966*(npP-ns),
   }
   samples={k:[] for k in variants};loops=250
   for fn in variants.values():
    for _ in range(10):fn()
   names=list(variants)
   for repeat in range(7):
    for k in names[repeat:]+names[:repeat]:
     fn=variants[k];threads.verify_thread_policy();cpu=time.process_time();wall=time.perf_counter()
     for _ in range(loops):value=fn()
     elapsed=time.perf_counter()-wall;cpu_elapsed=time.process_time()-cpu;threads.verify_thread_policy()
     samples[k].append({'ns_per_call':elapsed*1e9/loops,'cpu_ns_per_call':cpu_elapsed*1e9/loops})
   ref=variants['torch_addmm']().numpy()
   details={}
   for k,fn in variants.items():
    value=fn();arr=value.numpy() if isinstance(value,torch.Tensor) else value
    vals=[r['ns_per_call'] for r in samples[k]]
    details[k]={'samples':samples[k],'median_ns':statistics.median(vals),'min_ns':min(vals),'max_ns':max(vals),'sha256':hashlib.sha256(np.ascontiguousarray(arr).tobytes()).hexdigest(),'maxabs_vs_addmm':float(np.max(np.abs(ref-arr))) if not any(s in k for s in ('tanh','lerp','leak')) else None}
   output['rows'].append({'batch':batch,'weight_strides':list(W.stride()),'state_strides':list(st.stride()),'results':details})
 with (BASE/'primitives-result.json').open('x') as f:json.dump(output,f,indent=2)
 print(json.dumps({r['batch']:{k:round(v['median_ns']/1000,3) for k,v in r['results'].items()} for r in output['rows']}))

stage_script.source:
"""Stage the published CPU diagnostic with stdlib only; never run numerical work.

Example (use the exact public JSON and an exclusive new output directory):
  python -S reconstruct_cpu_profile.py --publication DATA.json \
    --repository /path/to/ResDAG --output /path/to/new-run \
    --numerical-python /path/to/pinned-env/bin/python

This extracts embedded scripts, archives the fixed Git commit (never the working
runtime), restores the probe's expected protocol and verifies all input hashes.
It prints the four numerical commands in order, but does not execute them.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import io
import json
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

FROZEN_COMMIT = "3b34005efd93a2f6573ecd96c9a5b23daecdf547"
SCRIPT_NAMES = {"_threads.py", "probe.py", "primitives.py", "b4_workflow.py", "csr_workflow.py"}
NUMERICAL_MODULES = {"numpy", "scipy", "torch", "resdag", "pytorch_symbolic", "networkx", "threadpoolctl"}


def digest(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def canonical(value) -> str:
    return digest(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True).encode())


def require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def validate(publication: dict) -> None:
    source = publication["source"]
    require(source["commit"] == FROZEN_COMMIT, "Unexpected frozen source commit")
    require(canonical(source["files"]) == source["manifest_sha256"], "Source manifest hash mismatch")
    require(set(publication["scripts"]) == SCRIPT_NAMES, "Expected exactly the five captured scripts")
    for name, entry in publication["scripts"].items():
        require(digest(entry["source"].encode()) == entry["sha256"], f"Script hash mismatch: {name}")
    for collection in ("native_policies", "import_origin_manifests"):
        for expected, value in publication[collection].items():
            require(canonical(value) == expected, f"Invalid {collection} receipt hash")
    for row in publication["initial_attribution"]:
        require(row["probe_sha256"] == publication["scripts"]["probe.py"]["sha256"], "Initial probe binding differs")
        require(row["source_manifest_sha256"] == source["manifest_sha256"], "Initial source binding differs")
    require(publication["primitive_diagnostic"]["probe_sha256"] == publication["scripts"]["primitives.py"]["sha256"], "Primitive script binding differs")
    for kind, name in (("b4", "b4_workflow.py"), ("csr-bridge", "csr_workflow.py")):
        for process in publication["whole_workflow_diagnostics"][kind]["processes"]:
            require(process["probe_sha256"] == publication["scripts"][name]["sha256"], f"Diagnostic script binding differs: {kind}")
            require(process["source_manifest_sha256"] == source["manifest_sha256"], f"Diagnostic source binding differs: {kind}")
    staged = publication["reproduction"]["stage_script"]
    require(digest(staged["source"].encode()) == staged["sha256"], "Reconstruction source hash differs")
    require(digest(Path(__file__).read_bytes()) == staged["sha256"], "This reconstruction script differs from the embedded copy")


def extract_archive(archive: bytes, destination: Path) -> None:
    # Explicit extraction also supports early Python 3.11 without tar filters.
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(archive)) as source:
        members = source.getmembers()
        for member in members:
            path = PurePosixPath(member.name)
            require(not path.is_absolute() and ".." not in path.parts, "Unsafe archive path")
            require(path.parts[:2] == ("src", "resdag") or str(path) == "src", "Unexpected archive prefix")
            require(member.isdir() or member.isfile(), "Symlinks and special archive members are unsupported")
        for member in members:
            target = destination.joinpath(*PurePosixPath(member.name).parts)
            if member.isdir():
                target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            else:
                target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                stream = source.extractfile(member)
                require(stream is not None, "Missing archive payload")
                with target.open("xb") as output:
                    output.write(stream.read())


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--publication", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--repository", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True, help="must not already exist")
    parser.add_argument("--numerical-python", default=sys.executable, help="printed only; not executed")
    parser.add_argument("--expected-publication-sha256", help="optional independent download checksum")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    require(not (NUMERICAL_MODULES & sys.modules.keys()), "Numerical packages were already imported; invoke this staging script with python -S")
    raw = args.publication.read_bytes()
    if args.expected_publication_sha256:
        require(digest(raw) == args.expected_publication_sha256, "Publication file checksum differs")
    publication = json.loads(raw)
    validate(publication)
    repository = args.repository.resolve(strict=True)
    commit = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "--verify", FROZEN_COMMIT + "^{commit}"], cwd=repository, text=True).strip()
    require(commit == FROZEN_COMMIT, "Repository resolved a different commit")
    archive = subprocess.check_output(["git", "archive", FROZEN_COMMIT, "src/resdag"], cwd=repository)
    output = args.output.resolve()
    output.mkdir()  # Exclusive: never overwrite an existing experiment.
    extract_archive(archive, output / "source")
    actual = {path.relative_to(output / "source").as_posix(): digest(path.read_bytes()) for path in sorted((output / "source").rglob("*.py"))}
    require(actual == publication["source"]["files"], "Archived runtime files differ from the full published manifest")
    for name, entry in publication["scripts"].items():
        with (output / name).open("xb") as stream:
            stream.write(entry["source"].encode())
        require(digest((output / name).read_bytes()) == entry["sha256"], f"Written script differs: {name}")
    protocol = dict(publication["protocol"])
    protocol.update(source_files=publication["source"]["files"], manifest_sha256=publication["source"]["manifest_sha256"], source_commit=FROZEN_COMMIT, runtime_reference=publication["source"]["runtime_reference"])
    with (output / "protocol.json").open("x") as stream:
        json.dump(protocol, stream, indent=2)
        stream.write("\n")
    require(json.loads((output / "protocol.json").read_text()) == protocol, "Written protocol differs")
    commands = [[args.numerical_python, str(output / name)] for name in ("probe.py", "primitives.py", "b4_workflow.py", "csr_workflow.py")]
    with (output / "RUN_IN_ORDER.txt").open("x") as stream:
        stream.write("After installing pinned dependencies, with no competing benchmark or test workload, run serially on the declared macOS host; do not launch these together.\n\n")
        stream.write("\n".join(shlex.join(command) for command in commands) + "\n")
    require(not (NUMERICAL_MODULES & sys.modules.keys()), "Staging imported a numerical package")
    receipt = {"schema": "cpu-profile-reconstruction-v1", "publication_sha256": digest(raw), "frozen_commit": commit, "archive_sha256": digest(archive), "source_files": len(actual), "source_manifest_sha256": canonical(actual), "script_sha256": {name: digest((output / name).read_bytes()) for name in sorted(SCRIPT_NAMES)}, "protocol_canonical_sha256": canonical(protocol), "numerical_modules_imported": [], "numerical_commands_executed": False, "commands_in_order": commands}
    with (output / "reconstruction-receipt.json").open("x") as stream:
        json.dump(receipt, stream, indent=2)
        stream.write("\n")
    print(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

reproduction.frozen_archive: git archive 3b34005efd93a2f6573ecd96c9a5b23daecdf547 src/resdag; manually extracted under OUTPUT/source, never copied from the current checkout runtime.

environment.version_boundary: Python/Torch/NumPy/SciPy versions were captured by the original numerical workers. Additional core/thread-helper pins were checked from the same project-venv distribution metadata while preparing this reconstruction; no numerical packages were imported by that metadata check. Pin versions do not imply identical vendor builds or hardware. Original native build/configuration receipts are included.
environment.platform: Staging needs Git and stdlib Python only. Actual saved probes currently require macOS because they call pmset -g therm and pmset -g batt at boundaries; strict helper requires observed vendor APIs, including BLASSetThreading/BLASGetThreading on Accelerate (macOS15+). Captured system was AppleM5/macOS27.0.1. A Linux run needs an explicitly different condition-receipt implementation and is not this exact script.
environment.resdag_install: Do not pip-install the working checkout for this experiment. Workers prepend OUTPUT/source/src and verify imported frozen-runtime origins. Other runtime dependencies must already be installed in the dedicated numerical environment.
environment.optional_dependencies: No Optuna/HPO, ReservoirPy, Julia, TSDynamics or compiler is needed. Pip may install Torch/core transitive dependencies; their build provenance can affect regeneration.
example_environment_setup: /absolute/path/profile-env/bin/python -m pip install torch==2.10.0 numpy==2.4.6 scipy==1.17.0 pytorch-symbolic==1.2.1 networkx==3.6.1 threadpoolctl==3.6.0

steps: Save reproduction.stage_script.source verbatim as reconstruct_cpu_profile.py; verify its UTF8 SHA256 equals reproduction.stage_script.sha256. Keep this publication JSON and a Git repository containing the full frozen commit.

Prepare a dedicated environment with the declared pinned dependencies; do not run these commands inside an environment doing another numerical workload. Dependency installation is separate from the stdlib staging script.

Run: python -S reconstruct_cpu_profile.py --publication /absolute/path/phase-five-cpu-recurrence-2026-10-23.json --repository /absolute/path/ResDAG --output /absolute/path/NEW-EXPERIMENT --numerical-python /absolute/path/profile-env/bin/python . Optional --expected-publication-sha256 checks an independently published whole-file checksum. OUTPUT must not exist.

Inspect reconstruction-receipt.json: all205 runtime file hashes, source manifest, all5 captured script hashes, native/import receipt bindings and diagnostic script bindings are verified. protocol.json now contains source_files and manifest_sha256 in the locations expected by the captured probe. Staging executes no numerical command/import.

After installing pinned dependencies, with no competing benchmark or test workload, execute RUN_IN_ORDER.txt serially: probe.py, then primitives.py, then b4_workflow.py, then csr_workflow.py. Do not run in parallel. The first script creates the fixed weights/data required by later scripts.

Each script writes exclusive outputs and retains failures/warnings. To repeat, reconstruct into another new directory; do not delete/retry failed timing artifacts or overwrite existing receipts. Compare raw times/hashes with the publication, remembering that bit-identical regeneration and speed across vendor builds/hardware are not guaranteed.
reproduction.verification_boundary: Reconstruction was tested as a staging operation only. No numerical probe was rerun to validate this recipe; the actual captured experiment remains the original evidence.
